question: Should imsg adopt `send-sticker` and `send.sticker` as a maintained advanced-bridge contract backed by private IMCore behavior, and is local runtime/database proof sufficient without a recipient-side capture?
rationale: Code review can assess the guarded implementation but cannot choose the long-term private-framework support commitment or acceptable end-to-end proof standard for a new public API.

options.title: Adopt after recipient proof
options.body: Accept the guarded API after adding redacted recipient-side evidence that standalone and attached stickers render correctly on the exact head.

options.title: Accept current proof
options.body: Adopt the API with the current live and database evidence while explicitly owning private-IMCore compatibility risk.

options.title: Decline the API
options.body: Keep sticker metadata reading but do not add a maintained native sticker-send surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt after recipient proof
recommendation.body: Accept the guarded API after adding redacted recipient-side evidence that standalone and attached stickers render correctly on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest merged ownership of the native bridge and authored the final contract and trust-boundary rewrite.
